traits.limb_angle.note: Sargent's Manual (sargent-1922, p. 345): 'rather small spreading branches'.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS's southern magnolia review (Coladonato 1991, read 2026-10-16): "grows 60 to 90 feet (18-27 m) tall". Silvics (p. 446) reports 30 to 38 m in Florida; FNA vol. 3 gives trees to 37 m.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Magnolia grandiflora (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): blade (7.5-)13-20(-26) cm long.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Magnolia grandiflora (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): blade (4.5-)6-10(-12.5) cm wide.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Flora of China vol. 7, Magnolia grandiflora (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): petiole 1.5-4 cm.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Magnolia grandiflora (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): blade narrowly to broadly elliptic or oblanceolate, thick and leathery.

traits.leaf_habit.note: FEIS's southern magnolia review (Coladonato 1991, read 2026-10-16): "a fast-growing, medium-sized, native evergreen tree".

traits.architectural_model.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 477, Magnolia grandiflora: the book's example of Fagerlind's model.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Magnolia grandiflora (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): flowers 15-30(-45) cm across.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Flora of China vol. 7, Magnolia grandiflora (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): tepals 9-12, so three or four whorls of three.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 201, Magnolia grandiflora: a cupped flower of many tepals.

traits.flower_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Magnolia grandiflora (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): tepals creamy white. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.stamens.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Magnolia grandiflora (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): stamens (179-)213-383(-405).

traits.carpels.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Magnolia grandiflora (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): pistils (45-)55-81(-89).

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Magnolia grandiflora (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): a follicetum of beaked follicles; seeds with a red aril.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Magnolia grandiflora (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): follicetums 7-10 cm long.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 201, Magnolia grandiflora: the cone-like fruit rusty brown, red seeds hanging from the opened follicles. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.flowering_months.note: FEIS's southern magnolia review (Coladonato 1991, read 2026-10-16): flowers between April and June.

traits.fruiting_months.note: FEIS's southern magnolia review (Coladonato 1991, read 2026-10-16): fruit ripens from September through late fall.

generator.params.note: Pacific madrone's crown values (an evergreen broadleaf), changed by hand: one trunk, as FNA describes it (single-trunked), upright rather than leaning. Not fitted to measurements. spur_leaf is the leaf card the angiosperm rule gives leaf_size, 1.5 times the flora's mean blade, so short-shoot leaves are drawn the same size.

allometry.note: Silvics of North America vol. 2 (1990), Magnolia grandiflora (Outcalt), Growth and Yield p. 446: trees free of competition grow about 0.46 m in height and 0.76 cm in diameter a year to age 50, so about 23 m and 38 cm at 50 years.

appearance.note: By eye, after FNA vol. 3: grey bark in thick plates; thick, glossy, dark green leaves, rusty felted below.

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L117615), as no source read gives it.

traits.life_span.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L117615), as no source read gives it.

traits.rosette.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L117615), as no source read gives it.

traits.leaf_margin.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L117615), as no source read gives it.

traits.fruitlets.note: Woody Plant Seed Manual, Magnolia (read 2026-10-17): the fruit a cone-like aggregate of follicles, each splitting along its back on one or two seeds; FNA vol. 3 (via a SEINet mirror) 'follicetums cylindric to somewhat obovoid, follicles beaked'.

traits.fruit_seed_colour.note: Silvics of North America vol. 2, southern magnolia (read 2026-10-17): seeds 6-13 mm with a red coat emerge and hang on slender silken threads before dropping; WPSM: the sarcotesta bright red. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.perianth_parts.note: Flora of China vol. 7, Magnolia grandiflora (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): tepals 9-12, white, obovate, 6-10 x 5-7 cm, thickly fleshy; FNA vol. 3 (genus): tepals 9-15; Flora of Pakistan: perianth 9-15, concave.

traits.petal_shape.note: Flora of China vol. 7, Magnolia grandiflora (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): tepals obovate, 6-10 x 5-7 cm.

traits.petal_apex.note: Flora of China vol. 7, Magnolia grandiflora (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): tepals obovate, 6-10 x 5-7 cm, broadest near the tip; the tip is rounded (our reading of the outline).

traits.stamen_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Magnolia grandiflora (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): stamens 16-29 mm; Flora of China ca. 2 cm; Flora of Pakistan 1.25-2 cm.

traits.filament_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Magnolia grandiflora (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): filaments purple; Flora of Pakistan: filaments bright purple, anthers yellow. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.pistil_colour.note: iNaturalist photo 28372097 (mfeaver, obs 18545889, CC BY), a flower on its first day (read 2026-10-18): the carpel cone pale tan to yellow-green under its tomentum (Flora of China: gynoecium densely long tomentose). The colour is our reading of the photo.

traits.leaf_hairs_beneath.note: Flora of China vol. 7, Magnolia grandiflora (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): twigs, vegetative buds, petioles and leaf blade abaxial surfaces densely brown to grayish brown shortly tomentose.

traits.hair_colour.note: Woody Plant Seed Manual, Magnolia, table 2 (read 2026-10-18): southern magnolia's leaves evergreen, rusty brown and tomentose beneath; Flora of China: brown to grayish brown tomentose. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.anther_colour.note: Flora of China vol. 7, Magnolia grandiflora (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16); Flora of Pakistan (read 2026-10-18): anthers adnate, yellow, introrse; iNaturalist photo 28372097 (CC BY): the packed stamens cream to pale yellow on the first day. The colour is our reading of the words and the photo.

traits.bud_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Magnolia grandiflora (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): spathaceous bracts 2, leathery, outer bract abaxially brown to grayish pilose, inner bract densely brown to grayish pilose; Flora of Pakistan: bracts rusty tomentose. The bud shows the bracts until it opens. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.fruit_colour_ripening.note: Virginia Tech Dendrology, southern magnolia (read 2026-10-18): fruit an aggregate of follicles, green changing to red and later to brown; OSU Landscape Plants: rose-red aggregates. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.fruit_seed_thread_m.note: iNaturalist photos fetched with imagekit, batch inat-2026-10-18-2 (24 fruiting photos, read 2026-10-18): on the tree the red seeds sit in or just out of the split follicles (photos 459384287, 88469166, 98550635), dangling at most about their own length; Silvics: they hang on slender silken threads before dropping. The length, about 4 mm, is our reading of the photos.
